units.translation: 18 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Ῥοίτειον: “Ῥοιτιάδος ἔνδοθεν ἄκρης” (I 929). It is a promontory of Troy. (It is said to be from Rhoiteia, daughter of Proteus.) Choeroboscus spells it with the diphthong ει. — Tzetzes on Lycophron 200, 28. 338, 10 Sch.
18 the lemma is present in L

Abarnidos: Abarnis is a city of Lampsacus. It was named from the following cause. Aphrodite fell in love with Dionysus and had intercourse with him, and when he departed for India she had intercourse with Adonis. When Dionysus returned, she made a garland and went to meet him. And after crowning him she was ashamed to follow him because she was already married, but she withdrew to Lampsacus and wished to give birth to the child she was carrying by him. But Hera, out of jealousy, touched her belly with a bewitched hand and made her give birth to a misshapen child, who was called Priapus because Aphrodite denied him, and for this reason the place was called Aparnis. Later, by a change of letter, it was called Abarnis. Percote is a city of Troy, as Homer also says.

20 Etymologicum Genuinum (CD) Ἀβαρνίδα: as at I 932. Percote is a city of Troy, and Abarnis is a city of Lampsacus. It was named from the following cause. Aphrodite fell in love with Dionysus and had intercourse with him. When he departed for Media (India Reitz.), she married Adonis. When Dionysus returned, she made a garland and went to meet him, but she was ashamed to follow him because she was married, and she withdrew to Lampsacus and wished to destroy (give birth to Reitz.) the child she was carrying by him. But Hera, out of jealousy, touched her belly with a bewitched hand and made her give birth to a child, whom they say was named Priapus, ugly and with large genitals; and Aphrodite denied him, and from this the place was called Aparnis, and by a change of letter Abarnis. cf. Reitzenstein Gesch. d. griech. Etym. 1897, 318; W 96. Etymologicum Genuinum (A) Περκώτη: it is a city of Troy, and Περκώσιος is the citizen. cf. Reitzenstein l. l. 325. Stephanus of Byzantium Ἀβαρνος: ... Apollonius I 932–933 (ἠιόνα). Sophocles, in his commentary, relates that Aphrodite, having given birth to the misshapen Priapus in Lampsacus, denied him and called the region Aparnis, which by corruption is also called Abarnis. cf. W 90 Nonnus, abbot, on Gregory of Nazianzus, Against Julian II 34 (36, 1053 Migne) Suda Πρίαπος III Tzetzes on Lycophron 266, 1 Sch. cf. Hans Herter De Priapo 1932 (Rel.gesch. Vers. u.
